clue.text: Study party rules to begin with, being a high-flyer

parts.note: to con is an old verb meaning to study or learn by heart
a do is an informal word for a party

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word rules is wanted, as the phrase says

parts.note: the word rules supplies its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone cramming the rules of a political party before rising to the top of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High-flyer' suggests an ambitious person, but here it is literal: a large bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The condor is a huge vulture that soars at great altitude, a literal high-flying bird.

clue.text: Photo turned up on the woman's secret writing

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means read from the bottom, so the word is reversed

parts.note: pic is short for picture, a photo
her is the possessive for a woman

explanation.surface: A photo of a woman appearing with her coded diary.
explanation.definitionFit: A cipher is a code, a system for writing messages so outsiders cannot read them.

clue.text: Before mounting musical, director finally ran over story

indicators.note: before puts these pieces ahead of the musical in the answer
over means turned over, so the word ran is read backwards

parts.note: the word ran is used as written before being turned round

indicators.note: only the closing letter of the word director is used

parts.note: the word director supplies its closing letter

indicators.note: mounting in a down clue means going upwards, so the musical is read backwards

parts.note: Evita is the Lloyd Webber musical about Eva Perón

explanation.surface: A director rushing through a plot before putting on a show.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrative is an account of events, which is what a story is.

clue.text: Head removed from bygone sea creature

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, which is taken off here

parts.note: former means bygone, of an earlier time

explanation.surface: A beheaded fossil sea creature from ages past.
explanation.walkthrough: The ormer is an edible abalone found in the Channel Islands.
explanation.definitionFit: The ormer is a type of abalone, an edible shellfish living on rocky seashores.

clue.text: Lucky creature, not large, caressing Henry's cheek

indicators.note: the creature wraps itself around the letter for Henry, as if stroking it
not large means the letter for large is dropped from the creature

parts.note: a black cat is traditionally a sign of good luck in Britain
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A lucky small cat brushing against Henry's face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheek' looks like part of Henry's face, but it means insolence.
explanation.definitionFit: Backchat is impudent answering back, the same insolence that cheek means in British usage.

clue.text: Open-and-shut, according to the circumstances?

definitions.meaning: a cryptic sense: a suitcase may be open or shut
the plain sense: depending on what the situation turns out to be

explanation.walkthrough: 'Open-and-shut' looks like an easy legal case; it means a case (a suitcase) that can be either open or shut.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning whichever applies in the particular situation.

clue.text: Man entertaining yen to crush King Edward's army commander

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting, so the man holds the desire inside him

parts.note: Ken is a man's name
a yen is a longing, as is an itch
ER stands for Edwardus Rex, King Edward

explanation.surface: A man with an urge to defeat a king's general.
explanation.walkthrough: King Edward is also a potato variety, which makes 'crush' look like mashing; ER is Edwardus Rex.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Kitchener was the British field marshal who led the army in Sudan and was War Secretary in 1914.

clue.text: Ambassador having friendly relations with European poet

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador
to be in with someone is to be on friendly terms

explanation.surface: A diplomat on good terms with a European poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Heinrich Heine was a German Romantic poet whose verse Schubert and Schumann set to music.

clue.text: Miserly type drunk on whisky and Drambuie, principally

parts.note: tight is slang for drunk

indicators.note: principally means taking the chief, opening letter of each word

parts.note: these three words each supply their opening letter

explanation.surface: A skinflint getting drunk on Scotch and Drambuie.
explanation.walkthrough: Drambuie is a Scotch whisky liqueur.
explanation.definitionFit: A tightwad is slang for a stingy person who hates spending money, a miser.

clue.text: Defeated, running 20 for a specific nobleman

definitions.meaning: first meaning: knocked out, like a boxer who cannot rise
second meaning: away on an errand (20) for the Count

explanation.walkthrough: 20 refers to the answer at 20-across, a task involving travel; someone running one for the Count is literally out for him.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxer floored for a count of ten has lost, so the phrase means beaten or unconscious.

clue.text: Cardinal's assistant, initially receiving a rise

parts.note: PA stands for personal assistant

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word receiving is used

parts.note: the word receiving supplies its opening letter
taken as written
to mount is to rise or climb up

explanation.surface: A cardinal's aide getting promoted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' looks like a churchman; here it is the adjective meaning chief or principal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal as an adjective means of foremost importance, which is exactly what paramount describes.

clue.text: Scraggy girl's first obsession

parts.note: scraggy means thin and bony

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of the word girl

parts.note: the word girl supplies its opening letter

explanation.surface: A skinny girl's chief fixation.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a thing about something is to be obsessed with it, an informal idiom.

clue.text: Wagnerian heroine in the Valkyries? Yes and no

indicators.note: in tells us the name sits inside the words the Valkyries, across the gap between them

parts.note: the run of letters spans the end of the and the start of Valkyries

explanation.surface: A quiz question: is this Wagner heroine one of the Valkyries?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yes and no' is the joke: the name is in the words 'the Valkyries', but the character is not in Die Walküre; she is the heroine of Die Meistersinger.
explanation.definitionFit: Eva Pogner is the heroine of Wagner's opera Die Meistersinger von Nürnberg.

clue.text: Right setting for English first-year students providing elevenses, perhaps?

indicators.note: the abbreviation for right is a setting that holds the other pieces, as a mount holds a gem

parts.note: RT is an abbreviation for right, not just R
freshmen are students in their first year at college

explanation.surface: A tutor laying on mid-morning snacks for new English undergraduates.
explanation.walkthrough: Right gives RT here, not the usual R. Elevenses is the British mid-morning snack or cup of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Elevenses is a light snack taken mid-morning, an example of the food and drink called refreshment.

clue.text: Root retired man associated with mother's ruin

parts.note: a traditional British nickname for gin

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: Reg is a man's name, short for Reginald

explanation.surface: A pensioner whose downfall is linked to gin drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Root' looks like a verb or a cause; it is the noun for the spice.
explanation.definitionFit: Ginger is the pungent underground rhizome of a tropical plant, used as a spice, so a root.

clue.text: Newlywed crosses stream, finding place to eat

indicators.note: crosses means the newlywed spans the stream, which sits inside him

parts.note: a groom is a man just married
a rill is a small stream

explanation.surface: A bridegroom fords a brook and finds a restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: A grillroom is a restaurant or dining room serving grilled food.

clue.text: Forgetfulness of men travelling in continent

indicators.note: in puts the rearranged men inside the continent

parts.note: Asia is a continent

indicators.note: travelling suggests the letters of men moving about into a new order

parts.note: the word men is used as written, its letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Men touring a continent who forget things.
explanation.definitionFit: Amnesia is loss of memory, the medical name for extreme forgetfulness.

clue.text: Opera with spoken dialogue, one mostly including a lot of agents

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step
mostly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: single means one

indicators.note: a lot of the word, but not all, so its last letter goes

parts.note: spies are secret agents

explanation.surface: A single opera singer surrounded by a crowd of spies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Including' tells you the agents go inside the shortened word for one.
explanation.definitionFit: Singspiel is a German form of light opera, like Mozart's Magic Flute, mixing songs with spoken dialogue.

clue.text: Outstandingly fine method of punishment!

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a smacking on the bottom

explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark points to the comic clash between the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanking is informal for striking and excellent, and also the act of smacking a child as discipline.

clue.text: Petulant woman feeding wandering sheep

indicators.note: feeding means the woman goes inside, as food goes into a mouth
wandering sheep are scattered, so the word sheep is rearranged

parts.note: the word sheep is used as written, its letters to be rearranged
Vi is a woman's name, short for Violet

explanation.surface: A cross woman feeding stray sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Petulant and peevish both describe someone childishly irritable and bad-tempered.

clue.text: Make a mistake with task involving travel

parts.note: to err is to make a mistake
and can stand in for with, both meaning together

explanation.surface: Getting something wrong with a job that needs a trip.
explanation.definitionFit: An errand is a short trip to do a job for someone, such as fetching shopping.

clue.text: Finally seeing publicity, obtain gizmo

indicators.note: only the last letter of the word seeing is used

parts.note: the word seeing supplies its closing letter
an ad, an advertisement, is publicity
to get is to obtain

explanation.surface: Finally spotting an advert and buying a gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: A gizmo is an informal word for a clever little device, the same as a gadget.

clue.text: Recent deal sadly restricting fine sewing and embroidery

indicators.note: restricting means the rearranged letters hem in the letter for fine
sadly suggests the words recent deal have gone wrong, so they are rearranged

parts.note: these two words are used as written, their letters to be rearranged
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A disappointing new contract limiting a craft business.
explanation.definitionFit: Needlecraft is the umbrella name for crafts done with a needle, which sewing and embroidery are.

clue.text: Eg wide passage out, not one taken by painter

indicators.note: the shortened word is taken up by the painter, who follows it
not one means the letter for one is left out

parts.note: an exit is a way out
RA is a Royal Academician, a painter

explanation.surface: A wide corridor leading out that a painter didn't use.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a wide is a ball bowled out of the batter's reach, and the run it gives is one of the extras.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, extras are runs not scored off the bat, and a wide is one type.

clue.text: Foul smell left by small fish

indicators.note: left by means the letter for small has departed from the word

parts.note: a stench is a foul smell

explanation.surface: A bad odour left behind by a tiny fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The tench is a freshwater fish of the carp family found in European ponds.

clue.text: Afterthought about a source of spring water

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the postscript is read backwards

parts.note: PS, a postscript, is an afterthought at the end of a letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A postscript added about a mineral spring.
explanation.definitionFit: A spa is a mineral spring, or a town built around one, whose water people drink or bathe in.

clue.text: Keen on adopting Rachmaninoff's first prelude

indicators.note: adopting means taking in, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: to be into something is to be keen on it

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of the composer's name

parts.note: the composer's name supplies its opening letter

explanation.surface: A pianist fond of taking up Rachmaninoff's first prelude.
explanation.walkthrough: Rachmaninoff's Prelude in C sharp minor makes 'prelude' look like music, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is the opening section of something, so a short prelude or introduction.

clue.text: Hardline barrister initially involved in interminable case

indicators.note: involved in means placed inside the next word

parts.note: interminable means unending, never coming to a stop

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word barrister is used

parts.note: the word barrister supplies its opening letter

explanation.surface: A tough lawyer stuck on a case that never ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' completes the courtroom picture and plays no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Unbending means refusing to compromise or yield, the attitude a hardline person takes.

clue.text: Flyer's attempt at test taking hours

indicators.note: taking means the test is followed by and takes on the hours

parts.note: a go is an attempt
taken as written
the MOT is Britain's annual roadworthiness test for vehicles

explanation.surface: A pilot's try at a test that lasts for hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flyer' suggests an aviator; it is a winged insect. The MOT is the annual safety test for British cars.
explanation.definitionFit: The goat moth is a large moth whose caterpillars smell of goat, and any moth is a flying insect.

clue.text: Court housing able-bodied in Swiss Cottage?

indicators.note: housing means the court abbreviation holds the next word inside it

parts.note: hale means healthy and strong

explanation.surface: A court case about the able-bodied in Swiss Cottage, a district of London.
explanation.walkthrough: Swiss Cottage is an area of north London, which makes it look like a place name.
explanation.definitionFit: A chalet is the wooden house typical of the Alps, so literally a Swiss cottage.
